zebralogic.title: Assign fixed‑position attributes immediately
zebralogic.principle: If a clue directly states that a specific attribute value belongs to a particular house number, assign that value to that house right away and remove it from all other houses.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue contains a phrase like “in the first house”, “in house 5”, or “the third house” that ties an attribute to a house number.
zebralogic.example: Assigning the country music to house 2 despite the clue “The person who loves country music is in the first house”.

zebralogic.title: Translate direct adjacency into offset constraints
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says X is directly left/right of Y, enforce that X and Y occupy adjacent houses with X’s position = Y’s position − 1 (or + 1).
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses “directly left of”, “directly right of”, “immediately left/right of”, or similar wording.
zebralogic.example: Treating “The person who loves jazz music is directly left of Eric” as a non‑adjacent ordering, allowing other houses between them.

zebralogic.title: Interpret distance clues correctly
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says there are N houses between X and Y, enforce that the absolute difference in their positions equals N + 1 (|pos(X) − pos(Y)| = N + 1).
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue contains “N houses between”, “two houses between”, “exactly three houses between”, etc.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting “There are two houses between Arnold and the Victorian house” as Arnold being directly next to the Victorian house.

zebralogic.title: Bind equivalence clues to the same house
zebralogic.principle: If a clue equates two attribute values (e.g., “The photographer has gray hair”), treat them as belonging to the same house, linking the attributes together.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses “is”, “has”, or similar linking verbs to connect two attributes.
zebralogic.example: Failing to link “Carol is the person who loves hip‑hop music” with “The person in a Mediterranean‑style villa loves hip‑hop music”, resulting in separate assignments for Carol’s music and house style.

zebralogic.title: Treat 'somewhere left/right of' as inequality
zebralogic.principle: Clues that say X is somewhere left/right of Y impose only an ordering (pos(X) < pos(Y) or pos(X) > pos(Y)), without requiring adjacency.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue contains “somewhere to the left of”, “somewhere to the right of”, “to the left of”, or “to the right of” without the word “directly”.
zebralogic.example: Treating “hip‑hop is somewhere left of knitting” as “hip‑hop is directly left of knitting”, placing them adjacent and breaking other constraints.

zebralogic.title: Apply exclusion constraints
zebralogic.principle: When a clue forbids an attribute from a specific house (e.g., “Eric is not in the second house”), eliminate that possibility from that house and keep it unavailable for all other houses.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue contains “not”, “cannot be”, “does not live in”, or similar negation.
zebralogic.example: Allowing Eric to be placed in house 2 despite the clue “Eric is not in the second house”.

zebralogic.title: Enforce uniqueness across each attribute category
zebralogic.principle: Each value in a category must appear exactly once across all houses; after assigning a value to a house, remove it from the candidate sets of all other houses.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Continuously throughout solving, after any assignment.
zebralogic.example: Assigning the same music genre to two different houses, violating the uniqueness rule.

zebralogic.title: Preserve original case of attribute values
zebralogic.principle: When outputting the final solution, write each attribute value exactly as it appears in the problem statement, preserving capitalization, hyphens, and spelling.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: During final answer formatting, before sending the JSON response.
zebralogic.example: Outputting “Hip hop” instead of the exact “hip‑hop” as given in the problem.

zebralogic.title: Make forced assignments when only one candidate remains
zebralogic.principle: If after applying all constraints a house (or an attribute) has exactly one possible remaining value, assign it immediately.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: After each round of constraint propagation, check for singleton candidate sets.
zebralogic.example: Not assigning the only remaining hobby to a house when all other possibilities have been eliminated, leaving the puzzle underdetermined.

zebralogic.title: Interpret phrasing 'There is one house between X and Y' as a distance clue
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says “There is one house between X and Y” (or similar wording), enforce that the positions differ by exactly two houses (|pos(X) − pos(Y)| = 2). This prevents treating the clue as simple adjacency.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue mentions “one house between”, “exactly one house between”, or “a single house between” two entities.
zebralogic.example: Treating “There is one house between the painter and the colonial house” as adjacency, placing them next to each other, which violates the clue.

zebralogic.description: Treating 'somewhere left/right of' as adjacency (directly left/right)
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model confuses ordering clues with adjacency, assuming immediate proximity.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Interpret 'somewhere left/right of' as a strict ordering constraint without requiring adjacency.

zebralogic.description: Interpreting 'N houses between' as distance N
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model subtracts N instead of adding one, treating the clue as adjacency for N = 1.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: When a clue says 'N houses between', enforce |pos(X) − pos(Y)| = N + 1.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring equivalence clues that bind two attributes to the same house
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model treats linked attributes as independent, missing the equality constraint.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: When a clue equates two attributes, enforce they share the same house.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model fails to remove assigned values from other houses, allowing duplicates.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: After assigning a value, eliminate it from the candidate sets of all other houses.

zebralogic.description: Assuming a fixed direction for 'next to each other' clues
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model interprets 'next to each other' as X left of Y, ignoring the bidirectional nature.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Treat 'next to each other' as unordered adjacency; either X left of Y or Y left of X is allowed.
